page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-16xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processors. It features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at a high clock speed of 3.9 GHz, supported by 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, and the system includes 60 MB of L3 cache. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is established at a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r7iz.metal-16xl demonstrates top-tier performance, particularly in single-core and multi-core Geekbench tests, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. This high compute capability is reinforced by strong memory bandwidth, with read-only small block cached memory bandwidth reaching 5705.78 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 106.24 GB/sec. Database operations via Passmark also rank in the top 10%, while Redis SET operations achieve 85.67 million operations per second. The server's hardware acceleration features, such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions, support efficient execution of complex mathematical and cryptographic tasks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.metal-16xl offers a high-density resource profile that balances massive DDR5 memory capacity with high-frequency CPU cores, reducing the need to compromise between compute speed and memory scale. However, the lack of local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent data. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive and compute-heavy workloads, including large-scale database operations, software compilation, real-time data processing, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-16xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server featuring 64 vCPUs powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processors running at 3.9 GHz. The server excels in performance, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores ranking in the top 10% tier. It also achieves top-tier results in Passmark database operations and image processing. Supported by Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, the hardware delivers strong memory bandwidth and high-throughput Redis operations. This configuration is highly efficient for workloads requiring both high-frequency compute and large memory footprints, making it an excellent fit for enterprise databases, software compilation, and memory-intensive data processing.
